{warning}Please read [[Microsoft EWS to Graph Migration October 2026]] for details on the upcoming migration to Graph from Exchange via EWS.{/warning}
{warning}
For the best Microsoft Exchange and Microsoft Graph experience on desktop, we recommend Thunderbird 157 or newer.

Thunderbird on desktop implements Exchange via EWS (Exchange Web Services) and Microsoft Graph. Support for Exchange and Graph is '''currently limited to email'''.

Calendar and address book using Exchange and Graph on desktop will follow at a later date. Also in the future is Exchange and Graph support on Android, so please do not file bug reports for these items at this time.

For more technical detail, as well as things to test and look for, see the [https://wiki.mozilla.org/Thunderbird:Exchange Thunderbird:Exchange wiki page].{/warning}

__TOC__

=Setup=
When creating a new Exchange or Graph account, once an Exchange or Graph account is detected, Thunderbird will give you options for both Exchange and Graph.

==Configure your Exchange or Graph account==
Again, for the best experience, we recommend Thunderbird 157 or newer.
# Click the Thunderbird app menu {menu ☰} > {button New Account} > {menu Email}. The ''Account Hub'' dialog will appear.
# Enter your name, email address, and if required, your [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-factor_authentication two factor authentication code] for your Exchange or Graph email account.
# Click the {button Continue} button. The password entry dialog will appear in your system web browser.{note}'''Note:''' In the first dialog box, you do not enter your account password. You will enter your password in a separate, branded panel provided by Microsoft (not Mozilla) as part of their OAuth implementation.{/note} Screenshot of that panel provided by Microsoft:
#:[[Image:tb-141-oauth-microsoft-enter-password-win11|width=450]]
# Enter your password and click {button Sign in}. The account type selection dialog will appear.
#:[[Image:tb157-beta-exchange-graph-button|width=450]]
# Select the [[Image:radio_button|width=20]] {button Exchange} or the [[Image:radio_button|width=20]] {button Microsoft Graph API} radio button and click {button Continue} to use Thunderbird's built-in Exchange code.
# Follow the prompts to finish adding your Exchange or Graph account.
{note}'''Note:''' The {button Exchange} and {button Microsoft Graph API} radio buttons only appear if the email you entered is an Exchange or Graph account.{/note}

===Manual Exchange and Graph configuration===
There are a diversity of Exchange and Graph servers which could cause auto configuration of your Exchange or Graph email account to fail. Here's a potential workaround for that situation:
# Add a new email account: Thunderbird app menu {menu ☰} > {menu Add Account} > {menu Email}, enter a Microsoft 365 email address (e.g. <code>nemo@o365.thunderbird.net</code>) and then click '''MANUAL CONFIGURATION''' on the bottom left of the Account hub.
# Click {button Microsoft Exchange or Microsoft 365} and then click {button Set up account}.
# In the '''Exchange settings''' dialog, type one of the following URLs into the '''Enter the service URL''' field:
#* For EWS: https://outlook.office365.com/EWS/Exchange.asmx
#* For Graph: https://graph.microsoft.com/
# Click {button Find settings}. For EWS, '''Exchange Web Services''' will automatically be selected. For Graph, '''Microsoft Graph''' will be selected.
# Your Microsoft 365 email address (e.g. <code>nemo@o365.thunderbird.net</code>) you used in step 1 should be automatically entered into the '''Username''' field (if not, then correct it).
# Follow the prompts and fill in the settings from your Exchange or Graph administrator. Full details at [[Custom OAuth for advanced users]] (scroll down to '''Per-account OAuth2 Microsoft Exchange customization''').

=Send and receive emails with your Exchange or Graph Account=
Once you have configured your Exchange or Graph Account in Thunderbird, you can use it to [[Send and receive messages in Thunderbird|send and receive emails]] just like an IMAP or POP account.

=Limitations=
Not yet supported:
* Address book
* Calendar
* OAuth authentication with on-premise instances 
* Shared mailboxes

=Feedback and Bug Reports=
To report a problem when using version 157 or newer, please [https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/enter_bug.cgi?product=MailNews%20Core&component=Networking:%20Exchange&short_desc=%5BEWS%5D%20xxxxxxxxx&blocked=1847846&bug_type=defect file a bug report].

To see open bug reports and more technical detail about bug reporting, tracking bug activity, plus things to test and look for, see the [https://wiki.mozilla.org/Thunderbird:Exchange Thunderbird:Exchange wiki page].

You may use Topicbox to discuss or ask questions about Exchange, either the [https://thunderbird.topicbox.com/groups/beta beta group] or the [https://thunderbird.topicbox.com/groups/enterprise enterprise group].

=Microsoft hosted vs. self hosted Exchange and Graph servers=
Administrators and others interested in the details of EWS and Graph instances (Microsoft hosted, Microsoft hosted as tenant-specific, and self hosted) will want to refer to the [https://wiki.mozilla.org/Thunderbird:Exchange Thunderbird:Exchange wiki page] and [https://wiki.mozilla.org/Thunderbird:Microsoft_Graph_API Thunderbird:Microsoft_Graph_API wiki page].
